**Setup.** Let $f(n)=v_7(n!)$ be the number of base-7 trailing zeros, and $g(n)=\left\lfloor v_2(n!)/3\right\rfloor$ the number of base-8 trailing zeros, since $8=2^3$. We need $f(n)=g(n)$.

**Small cases.** Using $v_2(n!)=n-s_2(n)$ and $v_7(n!)=\lfloor n/7\rfloor+\lfloor n/49\rfloor+\cdots$:

| $n$ | $v_2(n!)$ | $g(n)$ | $f(n)$ | Match? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1, 2, 3 | 0, 1, 1 | 0 | 0 | yes |
| 4, 5, 6 | 3, 3, 4 | 1 | 0 | no |
| 7 | 4 | 1 | 1 | yes |
| 8–11 | 7, 7, 8, 8 | 2 | 1 | no |
| 12–13 | 10, 10 | 3 | 1 | no |
| 14–15 | 11, 11 | 3 | 2 | no |
| 16–19 | 15, 15, 16, 16 | 5 | 2 | no |
| 20 | 18 | 6 | 2 | no |
| 21–23 | 18, 19, 19 | 6 | 3 | no |
| 24–27 | 22, 22, 23, 23 | 7 | 3 | no |
| 28–31 | 25, 25, 26, 26 | 8 | 4 | no |
| 32 | 31 | 10 | 4 | no |

Check $n=7$ directly: $7!=5040=7\cdot 720$ ends in one zero in base 7, and $5040=8\cdot 630$ with $630$ not divisible by 8, so it ends in one zero in base 8. ✓

**Large $n$.** Since $s_2(n)\le \log_2 n+1$, we have $g(n)\ge \frac{n-\log_2 n-1}{3}-1$. Since $s_7(n)\ge 1$, we have $f(n)\le \frac{n-1}{6}$. So $g(n)>f(n)$ whenever
$$\frac{n-\log_2 n-1}{3}-1>\frac{n-1}{6} \iff n>2\log_2 n+7,$$
which holds for all $n\ge 32$. The table already shows $g>f$ for $8\le n\le 32$.

Therefore the picante numbers are exactly $1, 2, 3, 7$. Since $2004$ is far beyond the bound (for instance, $g(2004)=665\neq 331=f(2004)$), all of them lie in $\{1,\dots,2004\}$.

**Count:** 4.

ANSWER: 4
